title.narrative: Enhancing the conservation and management of WH and TL sites in Palestine

description.narrative: Palestine, which accepted the World Heritage Convention on 8 December 2011, has five cultural properties inscribed on the World Heritage List: the Birthplace of Jesus (Church of the Nativity and the Pilgrimage Route, Bethlehem), inscribed in 2012; Palestine: Land of Olives and Vines (Cultural Landscape of Southern Jerusalem, Battir), in 2014; Hebron/Al-Khalil Old Town, in 2017; Ancient Jericho/Tell es-Sultan, in 2023; and Saint Hilarion Monastery/Tell Umm Amer, in 2024. Four of these are located in the West Bank and one in the Gaza Strip. In addition, the Palestinian Authority's submission of 14 new sites to UNESCO in January 2026 brought the total number of properties on its Tentative List to 24. Endorsed conservation and management plans have set out concrete action plans to strengthen the protection and management of these sites. Building on these frameworks, the activity will target support for the conservation of selected World Heritage and Tentative List properties, complementing conservation projects already under way and engaging youth as key actors in preservation, documentation, and awareness-raising. In doing so, it will help safeguard sites under pressure while building a generation of local stewards committed to protecting Palestinian heritage over the long term.
